M $100M Money Models · Scaling Workshop
Constraint Pipe · click any gate or lever, then “Show me how”
Draft 4 · executable

Your business is a pipe. Money flows only as fast as the tightest section.

Three sections: Supply (can you deliver more?), Conversion (do leads turn into sales?), Demand (do enough people want it?). Turn a knob to grow that section in steps of 10%. Throughput only rises when the tightest section rises: turn Supply up to 300% and nothing changes until Demand and Conversion follow. That is the constraint, and it's the only thing worth working on today.

Throughput = the lowest of the three · 100% = today
SupplyCapacity · manpower

The rule behind the pipe

There is only ever one constraint. Fix it, and the pipe grows until it hits the next one.

Widening a section that isn't the constraint changes nothing about the flow. That's why the drawing shows total flow as the narrowest point, not the sum.

Every business is demand-constrained in one of two ways: demand for customers, or demand for employees. Both get solved with the same four levers.

Demand · not enough people want it

Why can't we sell more?

Answer each gate honestly. The first "yes" is your exit. Get off there and do that one thing; don't keep driving.

You're here if

Calendar has gapsAds work but you can't scale spendLeads dried upSales team waiting on leadsCost per lead climbing
Decision walk · the Mozi Six (00:46:08)
Gate 1 · More Can we just do more of what already works?Double the ad spend. Double the outreach. Diminishing returns are still returns.
Gate 2 · Metrics Do we know our numbers?CAC, LTV, opt-in rate, close rate. No numbers, no diagnosis.
Gate 3 · Market Is the market really too small?"My market is too small" is one of the most common reasons Alex hears, and one of the least often true. Prove it with numbers first.
Gate 4 · Model Is it the model, or just the timeline?Changing the business you're in is a gigantic risk; most people plateau at the same spot again. Fix the timeline first.
Gate 5 · Money Which of the four money problems is it?Leads cost too much, you close too few, customers aren't worth enough, or the cash just comes in late.
Gate 6 · Manpower Could we even deliver it if we sold it?If not, you're on the wrong tab. Go to Supply.
Start at gate 1. If you can double the company with one thing, why do three?

Conversion · leads arrive, sales don't

Where in the funnel do they stop saying yes?

A funnel with a number at every step. Tap the band that leaks the most against industry average; that band is your constraint.

You're here if

Plenty of clicks, few opt-insBooked calls, low close rateLeads go cold before contactPrice objections every callSales fine but CAC too high
Leak finder · the funnel (02:21:45 · 04:06:27)
Band 1 · click → opt-in Is the opt-in offer worth a click?What is the actual opt-in offer, and when did you last test it?
Band 2 · opt-in → conversation Do we reach them while they're warm?Views become leads, leads become conversations. Minutes, not days.
Band 3 · conversation → sale Is our close rate below the industry?At 70% close you don't need conversion work; you need leads. Go to Demand.
Band 4 · sale → worth more Do they pay enough, and again?If they buy but it isn't worth enough, that's LTV, not conversion.
Band 1 of 4. Compare each step to industry average; the biggest gap is the leak.

Where it lives in the 4h25m recording

Supply · demand is there, you can't serve it

You're not short on customers. You're short on the people who serve them.

The bucket is full and overflowing. Open the right valve, in this order: price first, then structure, then hiring.

You're here if

Waitlist for servicesYou work 70+ hoursTurning away qualified customersQuality dropping with volumeStaff fully utilised, still behind
Valve order · flavours of supply constraint (02:04:33)
Valve 1 · Price Have we raised the price?More demand than supply means raise price. It's physics. Cash first.
Valve 2 · Structure Have we stretched what we have?Longer hours, more seats, faster turns, a better process.
Valve 3 · Applicants Not enough people applying?That's a lead problem. Same funnel, aimed at talent.
Valve 4 · Quality Applicants, but junk?Level up the avatar, or level down and add training.
Valve 5 · Money Can't afford them?Change wages, percentage, or the structure of the role itself.
Valve 1 of 5. Open the cheapest valve first; hiring is last.
